title: A short job at a New London beer joint
summary: Albertson asks for missed stories and he recalls a brief wartime job near the submarine yards with Wayman Carver.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes, well I want to get into the latin thing, but before we get into that, I'd like to go back and -- over what we have just talked about, last hour and a half or so, and see did we leave anything out, were there any interesting things that happened, back in those early days, say leading up to 1945? Any experiences that you --

There's was a little job I had up in New London, Connecticut, with Tiny -- Tiny whatever his name is, little job didn't mean anything, it was just doing -- during the war and submarines were being built up in New London.
No. This a bass player, he used to work around New York. I can't remember his name right now, it'll come to me.

He had a little job at a beer joint up there and Wayman Carver was playing flute and saxophone, Gary Lee on drums, and Tiny was a bass player. We had a little job over there -- short, short job didn't last too long. That's about the only thing of interest that happened. It was just a short thing, that was before I joined Eddie Heywood.
